summary: Nothing passed the proof rule this week, and the first live results are rough: all 7 settled lined-up buys hit their stop (-1R each) and Launch pick IT was stopped at -17%, with 3 of the last 9 Launch picks in the same group (IT Services). The big new tool is the trade warehouse with ~11 years of Yahoo history, which finally gives more than 2 deep thrusts to test on. Best next step: re-check the dashboard's core edges (post-thrust window, leading group, lifecycle BUY) on that 11-year history before building anything new on top of them.

items.title: Re-test the core edges on 11 years of history (warehouse step 2), then the stacked R
items.where: tools/warehouse (build.py / study.py on the 11-year Yahoo data, branch warehouse-data); later a stack line on launchPicksCard and lineupCard
items.how: Almost every edge we use was found on ~2 bull-heavy years with 6-7 thrusts. Put the lined-up dip trade (leader, first 9/21 ribbon dip, buy the dip-day-high break, stop the dip low, 20 sessions) into the 11-year warehouse with fixed columns: post-thrust window, leading group (top 30% on 60 days), lifecycle BUY, SPY above 50-day, strong breadth, volume tilt tier, extension at the leg high. Only the lifts that survive go into a stacked expected R shown on each live trade.
items.test: Pre-register the columns (same plan, grade 85%+ before outcomes). Each lift = R with minus without, per date, clustered by month, t 2+ and the same sign in both halves AND in pre-2024 vs 2024+. Stacked R then scored on the later half only: top fifth minus bottom fifth 0 and rank IC 0.05+.
items.kill: If the post-thrust or leading-group lift is about 0 before 2024, the lined-up / box edge is a 2-year artefact: drop those lifts from grades and say so on the cards. Stacked R with IC under 0.05: show proven single tags only.

items.title: Lined-up buys: 0 for 7 live, check the gate before trusting it
items.where: lifecycle layer, data/lineup_ledger.csv, lineupCard gate (buy / half / hold)
items.how: All 7 settled live trades (FIGS, FTRE, EOG, PTC, JNJ, VTRS, BILL) were stopped at -1R; 15 more didn't fill. With a 29% backtest win rate, 7 losses in a row happens about 1 time in 11, so it isn't proof yet. Check two things: what the gate said on those dates (they came during the late-October selloff, when breadth was weak and the backtest says BUY groups had no edge), and whether stops sit too tight versus the backtest (live fill = max(open, trigger)).
items.test: After 30 closed live trades: average R vs the +0.84R backtest and vs the weak-breadth subset of the backtest; same check split by gate state on the signal date.
items.kill: 30 closed trades with average R below 0 while the gate said buy: switch the card to 'hold off' until the 11-year re-test (item 1) is done.

items.title: Launch picks: one open pick per sub-theme across weeks
items.how: The rule is one pick per sub-theme each week, but open picks from earlier weeks don't count, so IT Services got IT, then CTSH, then CDW (IT stopped -17%), and Enterprise SaaS got ASAN then TEAM. With 13-week holds that stacks one group's risk. Proposal: skip a sub-theme that already has an open Launch pick (or cap at 2), and take the next name.
items.test: Run launch.replay both ways on every past week: average 13-week result vs SPY, worst drawdown of the open book, and t in both halves. Build only if the average is about the same or better (within 1 pt) and the worst open-book drawdown is smaller.
items.kill: Average drops more than 1 pt vs SPY or a half turns negative: keep the current rule (concentration in the leading group may be the edge).

items.title: After the Nov 4 thrust: 'broke out together' list + 21-EMA pullbacks in strong groups
items.where: info-only list next to the washout_thrust card (Breadth tab); playbook_state post-thrust window
items.how: Two new cards agree the edge is the 15-25 sessions after a thrust: fresh breakouts with 2+ sub-theme peers breaking out did +4.3% / +6.9% vs ordinary breakouts (t 4.1 / 2.5), and strong-group leaders that come back to the 21 EMA were a better buy than chasing (+0.37 to +0.60R, both halves). The 'special' 5-day jump added nothing. A Nov 4 thrust just printed, so this window is live until about Nov 25: build the list as information only and log it.
items.test: On the 11-year warehouse (many more thrusts): post-thrust peer-cluster breakouts vs ordinary breakouts, next open to 21 sessions, per thrust, both halves, t 2+; plus the card's open question: offensive vs defensive clusters (Apr 2025 defensives lost -8%).
items.kill: Edge under t 2 on 11 years, or only in deep thrusts (then fold it into the washout card).

items.title: Extension at the leg high and room to old peaks as dip penalties
items.where: lined-up buys and Best Setups nuzzle rows (a warning tag), via the warehouse
items.how: The weekly-dip test failed its main idea but left two leads: dips after a leg that ran 2.5+ weekly ranges over the weekly 21 EMA lost (-0.10R daily, -0.27R weekly), and dips with under 5% room to the next old peak lost on the daily entry (-0.25R). These are found, not proven. The magnets test was stopped by its power gate, so nothing there yet.
items.test: Pre-registered follow-up on the 11-year data (item 1 columns): extension top third vs rest, room under 5% vs rest, per date, clustered, both halves and both eras, t 2+.
items.kill: Either lead under t 2 or halves disagree: no tag.

items.title: Agent layers and live ledgers: first honest read about Nov 27
items.where: decision_log (catalyst, calendar, macro_brief), launch_ledger, trade_stories scorecard, washout_thrust
items.how: Nothing to build. Forward log: 249 settled ideas but only 11 dates; no agent layer is near t 2, and the macro brief has never said 'low risk', so it can't be tested. The Oct 15 shallow, 'unconfirmed' thrust is scored about Nov 13; log it as a case.
items.test: t 2+ over 20+ dates, same sign both halves.
items.kill: No agent layer reaches |t| 1 by about 100 more settled ideas: cut the catalyst agent to earnings checks only (saves ~20-40 searches a weekday).
